summary: Concurrent query limiter cancels long-running heatmap/dashboard analytics queries without actionable error
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that generation of a high-cardinality heatmap on the Console (Usage -> Heatmaps) is being cancelled after ~30s with an opaque 'Query cancelled' error. This happens consistently for broader time ranges (30+ days) and when the dashboard is exported using the customer's predefined 'Export: High-res analytics' preset.

Impact:
- Customer (Tempo Health Analytics) cannot produce weekly cohort heatmaps required for scheduled ops meetings.
- Reproducible across multiple user accounts at the customer's org and affects other enterprise tenants intermittently.
- Blocks scheduled reporting workflows and risks SLA breach for the customer's internal reporting commitments.

Environment and scope:
- Console UI in prod-us-east.
- Affects heatmap generation and CSV/PNG export flows triggered from dashboard -> Export with 'high-res analytics' preset.
- Observed primarily for customers on enterprise tier; self-serve customers rarely hit this due to smaller retention windows.

Observed behavior:
- UI shows spinner for ~25-35s then displays 'Query cancelled' toast. No guidance or retry link.
- Backend logs show cancellation originating from the query-orchestrator quota check. No matching 5xx from serving-runtime.
- Customer also reports that exporting the same view via API sometimes succeeds if broken into shorter date windows.

Desired behavior:
- Long-running analytics queries from Console heatmap/export flows should be allowed (or a clear error + recommended mitigations returned) for enterprise customers, or be transparently routed to batched/background export job with progress and notification.
steps_to_reproduce: Login to Console as enterprise user for Tempo Health Analytics (prod-us-east).
Navigate to Usage -> Heatmaps and select 'User Cohort Activity' with a time range of 60 days.
Select the 'Export' button and choose the preset 'Export: High-res analytics'.
Observe spinner for ~25-35s followed by 'Query cancelled' toast and no exported file in activity history.
Repeat using API export with the same time range: API request succeeds when split into three 20-day windows but fails when single request uses full 60-day window.
logs:
[2026-03-05T11:23:14Z] query-orchestrator: requestId=req_8f2b3 cancel_reason=concurrency_quota_exceeded tenant_id=tempo-health duration_ms=31240 preset=high-res-analytics
[2026-03-05T11:23:14Z] console-ui: user=tempo_user_3 toast='Query cancelled' export_preset=high-res-analytics
[2026-03-05T11:23:14Z] scheduler: enqueued background-export job=None (route=console-stream)
No 5xx from serving-runtime in same time window.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after customer reported reproducible failures during scheduled reports. Added logs and initial repro steps.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Liu (SRE): Acknowledged and set priority P1. Noted query-orchestrator emitted cancel_reason=concurrency_quota_exceeded. Asked for full tenant query rate history and any recent quota changes.

2026-03-06 - Tempo Health (Customer) via CS rep: Provided timestamps of scheduled exports and confirmed no recent change in their dashboard presets. They can reproduce immediately when sharing screen. Requested urgent workaround.

2026-03-07 - Marcus Liu (SRE): Temporary workaround suggested: reduce export time-range, or run exports via API split into <30s expected runtime chunks. Raising an ops request to increase concurrency cap for tenant 'tempo-health' to unblock scheduled reports.
2026-03-08 - Support (Aisha): Noted customer accepted temporary ops increase; asked Engineering for a permanent fix and better error messaging in Console.

2026-03-08 - Eng (callout): Creating PR to allow long-running analytics queries initiated from Console export presets to bypass short per-request concurrency bucket and instead be routed to a background export queue with progress updates. Refer to PR in linked_issues.
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: query-orchestrator enforces a conservative per-tenant concurrent query cap to protect serving runtime. Export presets with 'high-res-analytics' launch heavy aggregation queries that exceed the cap and are cancelled after the orchestrator's soft timeout (~30s). Evidence: cancel_reason=concurrency_quota_exceeded in logs and success when splitting into smaller time windows.

Things checked:
- Serving runtime logs: no OOMs or 5xx spikes.
- Scheduler: no background export attempts created automatically for console-triggered exports.
- Recent config changes: none applied to enterprise default concurrency on 2026-03-01.

Root cause hypothesis: mismatch between Console export UX (which expects synchronous export) and orchestrator's production concurrency policy. No clear user-facing guidance when cancellation occurs.

Next steps: create ops ticket to temporarily raise tenant concurrency; update UI to show 'Long-running analytics — exporting to background' option; implement orchestrator change to detect console-exported heavy queries and reroute them to background job queue with progress updates and Email/Console notifications.
resolution:
Workarounds provided: 1) Customer split export into smaller date windows via API; 2) Ops temporarily increased 'tempo-health' concurrency cap for 72 hours to allow backfilled exports.

Planned fix (Engineering):
- Short term (hotfix): Update query-orchestrator to allow console-initiated export presets a longer soft timeout and higher concurrency bucket for enterprise tenants (feature flag gated).
- Mid term: Implement background export job flow for heavy analytics exports triggered from Console; UX change to let users opt-in 'export to background with notification'.
- UX change: Replace opaque 'Query cancelled' toast with explicit message linking to KB article and offering 'Retry as background job' button.

Rollout notes: Hotfix behind feature flag will be rolled to prod-us-east on 2026-03-10 during a low-traffic window, monitored by Marcus Liu. Customer notified of temporary ops increase and planned hotfix schedule.
